name: Hard say-versus-do judgments
description: The six bundled records, each carrying the label one researcher gave it after reading both sources in full — written down before any model saw the pair, and not changed afterwards, so a disagreement here is a finding rather than a mislabel. None of the six is obvious from the two sentences alone: two are contradictions at the level of the mechanism rather than the goal (an association whose members pledged the outcome while it fought the compliance deadline; a bank whose pledge is denominated in the emissions it asked the regulator to delay disclosing), one reads exactly like a contradiction and is not (a pledge scoped to direct regulation, met by opposition to a separate charge), two are genuinely arguable (a pledge and an opposition that may not even be about the same object; a safety pledge vague enough that opposing one rule neither fits nor conflicts), and one is an organisation lobbying for the floor it already meets. These labels are one researcher's reading, not ground truth: the reasoning behind each is in app/seeds/data/sources/tutorial_say_versus_do.json, beside the quotes and links it was read from.
